note: Frozen v0.7.0 digital-engine registration baseline after Strategic Withdrawal plus the shared +Reserve/+Tactic implementation for Invasion, Liberation, and Reinforcements. Action parity remains 72/72; battle parity is 85/113, leaving 28 explicitly queued unsupported battle surfaces. The implementation distinguishes pre-choice Tactic-limit grants from post-reveal face-up additional Tactics, preserves the Counterattack condition, enforces Reinforcements' 'using that card' restriction, and retains Strategic Withdrawal's loss/retreat Aftermath behavior. The unsupported surface keys remain sorted and review-locked so registry drift fails Card Authority. Frozen v0.7.0 Underwriting battle registration adds its unchanged Gambit/Tactic surface after implementation against the shared Subsidize battle primitive, taking battle parity to 86/113 with 27 unsupported surfaces remaining. Divestment, Liquidation, and Margin Loan now use a shared reveal-pause procedure for their optional pre-dice economic effect followed by the printed immediate Subsidize window. Margin Loan binds face-up Hand/Treasury collateral and resolves Win-return versus Otherwise-Default in the Aftermath. Battle parity advances to 89/113 with 24 unsupported surfaces remaining. Corner the Market, Leveraged Buyout, and Monetary Crisis now participate in the shared controlled-Aftermath scheduler. Corner the Market recalculates Deed affordability after every purchase; Leveraged Buyout targets the contested Deed and routes selected battle collateral to the Graveyard during normal battle-card cleanup; Monetary Crisis resolves required Hand reductions in battle order within its single controlled effect. Battle parity advances to 92/113 with 21 unsupported surfaces remaining. Black Covenant now grants Advantage, opens its optional +1 Tactic from Hand as a face-up late additional Tactic, and routes both the Covenant and any chosen added Tactic to the Graveyard during Aftermath cleanup. Battle parity advances to 93/113 with 20 unsupported surfaces remaining. Guilt by Association now participates in the shared controlled-Aftermath scheduler; its controller chooses a title from the opponent's physical battle cards, moves every matching card currently in that opponent's Discard Pile to the Graveyard, and uses the normal Inquisition Aftermath Conviction trigger for those losses. Frozen battle parity advances to 94/113 with 19 unsupported surfaces remaining. Hellfire now resolves at its printed post-Tactics timing with a controller allocation of available Conviction between immediate Battle Total and a win-gated delayed Aftermath Draw-Pile loss; the delayed effect participates in shared controlled-Aftermath timing and uses the normal Inquisition Aftermath Conviction trigger for opposing cards actually lost there. Frozen battle parity advances to 95/113 with 18 unsupported surfaces remaining. Confession now resolves at its exact pre-normal-Tactic-reveal timing: it reveals itself if needed, reveals one opposing face-down Tactic subject to Counterintelligence, and may return itself to Reserve for another eligible face-down Tactic replacement. Frozen battle parity advances to 96/113 with 17 unsupported surfaces remaining. Scouting Report now resolves through the shared pre-normal-reveal scheduler at either Gambit or Tactic timing: it reveals one opposing face-down card at the same stage subject to Counterintelligence, then may replace itself from Reserve face up and goes to the Graveyard. The scheduler also preserves attacker/defender alternation and controller-selected ordering with Confession. Frozen battle parity advances to 97/113 with 16 unsupported surfaces remaining. Redemption now records qualifying opposing-effect Tactic negations centrally and resolves each active battle copy during the shared pre-clear Aftermath scheduler, returning one eligible negated Tactic that would otherwise enter the Discard Pile to its owner's Hand. Frozen battle parity advances to 98/113 with 15 unsupported surfaces remaining. Contraband now replaces itself at reveal timing with one currently executable same-role Gambit/Tactic from its controller's Discard Pile, moves the Contraband source to the Graveyard immediately, and defaults the replacement to the Graveyard in the Aftermath while preserving any explicit destination printed by the replacement card. Battle parity advances to 99/113 with 14 unsupported battle surfaces remaining. Operational Reassessment now resolves at its printed post-Tactics timing: a Gambit defers until Tactics are revealed, then its controller must either withdraw or replace the exact source with a same-role face-up Hand card whose registered battle timing can still resolve. Replacement moves the Reassessment source to the Graveyard, applies the replacement inside the existing reveal procedure, supports chained Reassessments, and leaves the replacement on its own normal printed cleanup path. Battle parity advances to 100/113 with 13 unsupported battle surfaces remaining. Paths of Shadow now resolves as a true replacement for the normal battle Retreat: the loss pauses before any Retreat is observed, the loser may move directly to another currently legal Territory they control, and declining falls through to the ordinary retreat. The replacement movement is not itself a Retreat, so Retreat +N modifiers and lose-and-retreat effects do not falsely trigger from it. Shared retreat observation now records actual normal/additional Retreat steps explicitly for existing Aftermath effects. Battle parity advances to 101/113 with 12 unsupported battle surfaces remaining. Reserve Force now resolves at its printed post-Tactics timing. A Gambit waits until that timing; the controller may choose zero, one, or two timing-eligible Hand replacements, each replacement inherits the source role and enters face up. Zero replacements keep Reserve Force in battle with an Aftermath Discard destination; any replacement puts Reserve Force in the Graveyard immediately. Replacement effects continue in order across nested reveal choices without reopening passed timing windows. Battle parity advances to 102/113 with 11 unsupported battle surfaces remaining. Hold the Line now resolves at its printed post-Tactics timing while defending a Territory the controller controls. It adds exactly two Reserve cards, grants an optional face-up additional Tactic restricted to those newly drawn cards, routes the active source to the Graveyard in the Aftermath, and registers the printed loss-after-retreat capture for the attacker through the shared contiguous Front Line capture procedure. Paths of Shadow replacement movement does not satisfy the actual-Retreat condition. Battle parity advances to 103/113 with 10 unsupported battle surfaces remaining. War Crimes now resolves as an optional shared-timing Aftermath effect. On a win, using it changes opposing Tactics' normal cleanup destination to Graveyard while preserving more-specific destination effects, applies Opponent: Retreat +1 only when the normal Retreat exists, puts the battle source in Graveyard, and imposes the printed no-movement/no-capture/no-Order restriction for that victory. Conflicting victory benefits are order-sensitive: an already-used victory-derived Order/capture makes War Crimes unavailable; War Crimes first suppresses later prohibited benefits. Battle parity advances to 104/113 with 9 unsupported battle surfaces remaining.
